This extract is complete for both regions across the full window (2026-02-01 through 2026-04-11): every region has exactly one row per calendar day, with no missing daily records.
# Rollout targeting note

West was selected for the checkout-flow rollout because it had the highest cart-abandonment complaint volume of any region in the quarter before rollout.

Cart-abandonment complaint counts, quarter before rollout (2025-11-01 through 2026-01-31):

# Concurrent UX cleanup

A separate, unrelated UX cleanup (form-field reordering on the shipping step) shipped to West gradually across the pre-rollout weeks and continued improving completion time in West through the whole pre-period, ahead of and independent of the checkout-flow rollout.
East did not receive this cleanup.
2026-03-15 West region-wide price promotion launched.
The promotion stacks a checkout discount on top of the existing loyalty discount, which is why average order value rises in West starting the same week as the checkout-flow rollout.
No promotion activity is recorded in East during this period.

item.text:
For the Q2 review, I’d report **a 50-second observed drop in West’s median daily checkout time, from 196.6 to 146.6 seconds, or about 25%**. East’s median held steady at about 180 seconds. **The data can’t isolate how much of West’s improvement came from the new checkout flow.**

West was already gaining on East by about half a second per day before launch, during a separate West-only UX cleanup. After extrapolating that pre-launch trend, West’s daily checkout times averaged **32 seconds below the projected level** over the four weeks after launch. A West-only price promotion began on launch day, so that gap can include effects from both changes. West was also selected because it had the most prior cart-abandonment complaints, which limits East’s usefulness as a comparison.

The post-launch window runs from March 15 through April 11. The extract covers only the first 11 days of Q2.
